newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Losses at Freegold shafts unsustainable.
newsitem.headline: Losses at Freegold shafts unsustainable.

text.p: Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd said on Thursday that losses at shafts within its Free State Consolidated Gold Mines Ltd unit were unsustainable and the shafts could be forced to close.
Available profit at Freegold slumped 43 percent to 62.9 million rand in the first quarter.

Of particular concern was the performance of three short/medium life shafts - Steyn Nos 2 and 5 and Freddies No 5 - and of the combined Western Holdings 2/3 shaft in the marginal category, the company said.

"Together, these shafts incurred a loss of some 18 million rand in the quarter. This magnitude of loss is unsustainable and on current performance these shafts will have to close," it said in a results statement.
Management at Freegold -- the world's biggest gold mine -- plans to discuss with unions as soon as possible ways in which the closures might be delayed or avoided.
Of the the long life shafts, only Freddies No 1 performed up to expectation and achieved productivity targets.
